summary: Atlassian's OAuth 2.0 (3LO) lets an external app access Jira or Confluence Cloud APIs on a user's behalf. You create and enable an OAuth 2.0 integration in the developer console, choose an account-level or resource-level grant, add scopes and a callback URL, then run the authorization code flow. No mandatory review is needed to build and distribute a 3LO app; listing in the Atlassian Marketplace is optional. Atlassian explicitly warns against instructing customers to create individual 3LO apps rather than shipping one distributable app.

steps.title: Create an OAuth 2.0 integration
steps.detail: In the developer console, choose Create and then OAuth 2.0 integration. Enter an app name and choose the OAuth 2.0 (3LO) grant type.

steps.title: Choose account-level or resource-level grant
steps.detail: Account-level consent can cover multiple sites where your app is installed; resource-level consent is limited to the specific site(s) the user selects. Pick based on how your app spans sites.

steps.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 (3LO), add scopes and callback URL
steps.detail: Under Authorization, enable OAuth 2.0 (3LO). Add the Jira/Confluence scopes your app needs and set the callback URL.
steps.gotcha: Building one distributable 3LO app is required by Atlassian's security requirements; instructing customers to create their own 3LO apps is non-compliant.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Direct the user to Atlassian's authorization URL with your client_id, scopes, and callback, exchange the returned code for an access token at the token URL, then call the Jira API with the token until it expires or is revoked.

notes: The callback URL is configured on the app and must match the authorization request.
Use the state parameter for CSRF protection in the authorization request.

recommended.purpose: Read Jira issues, projects, and related data.
Receive a refresh token for long-lived access.

sensitive.consequence: Administers Jira configuration; request only for admin tooling.
Creates and modifies issues on the user's behalf.

notes: Granular scopes are recommended over classic scopes; request only what each feature needs.
Include offline_access to obtain a refresh token.

blockers.title: Non-compliant per-customer 3LO apps
blockers.symptom: Customers are asked to create their own 3LO apps or API tokens.
blockers.cause: This pattern violates Atlassian's security requirements and acceptable use policy.
blockers.resolution: Ship a single distributable 3LO app and transition customers off custom 3LO apps/API tokens.

blockers.title: Token works for the wrong site
blockers.symptom: API calls fail or target an unexpected site.
blockers.cause: A resource-level grant limits the token to the specific site(s) the user selected.
blockers.resolution: Use an account-level grant if the app needs to span sites, or resolve the accessible resources for the token.

blockers.title: callback URL mismatch
blockers.symptom: Authorization fails on the redirect step.
blockers.cause: The callback URL does not match the one configured on the app.
blockers.resolution: Set the exact callback URL on the app and in the authorization request.
